channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Proposes Three Digital Cooperation Avenues for Central Asia
item.description: At the Second Tien Shan Forum in Almaty, Tajikistan's Agency for Innovation and Digital Technologies presented initiatives for digital economy and AI development. Three priority areas for regional cooperation were proposed: cross-border e-trade, joint youth internships, and utilizing Tajikistan's green computing power.

item.title: Kazakhstan's New Law Expands Islamic Banking Opportunities with Financial Monitoring
item.description: Kazakhstan's new 'On Banks and Banking Activity' law enhances Islamic finance by allowing universal banks to operate 'Islamic windows'. This move aims to integrate Islamic products, built on a different economic model, while ensuring compliance with financial monitoring requirements through separate accounting and asset management.

item.title: Osh to Construct Southern Bypass Road Spanning 32 Kilometers
item.description: The city of Osh will build a 32-kilometer southern bypass road, including an automotive highway, interchanges, and bridges. The project, formalized by a memorandum signed by the mayor, the minister of transport, and the road construction company director, aims to reduce city center traffic and improve road safety.

item.title: Kazakhstan Uses Only 3.5% of Underground Water Reserves, Lawmaker Demands Audit
item.description: A lawmaker in Kazakhstan has called for an inventory of underground water resources, citing that only 3.5% of the estimated 43.2 million cubic meters per day are currently utilized. The proposal includes modernizing monitoring systems, creating a digital registry of abandoned wells, and establishing usage limits, particularly for agriculture.

item.title: Kazakhstan Lawmaker Proposes Occupying New Buildings Only After Social Facilities Open
item.description: A proposal in Kazakhstan suggests linking the occupancy of new housing developments to the scheduled opening of essential infrastructure, including roads and social facilities like schools and clinics. This aims to prevent new districts from becoming overcrowded "human anthills" lacking basic services and to improve urban integration.

item.title: Eight Kazakh Citizens Remain Hospitalized in Tashkent After Mass Poisoning Incident
item.description: Eight citizens of Kazakhstan, including six children and two adults, are still receiving treatment in Tashkent hospitals following a mass poisoning incident. Their condition is stable, and they are receiving necessary medical care. A total of 18 Kazakh citizens were hospitalized after the incident, which occurred on November 2.

item.title: Kazakhstan Foils Attempt to Smuggle 11 Red Book Falcons Abroad
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Border Service has stopped an attempt to illegally smuggle 11 protected Red Book falcons out of the country. The incident occurred on October 31 in the Turkistan region. A Kazakhstani citizen was detained, and the birds are valued at over 100 million tenge on the black market.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Build Samarkand-Bukhara Toll Road, Reducing Travel Time
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to construct a new toll road between Samarkand and Bukhara, significantly cutting travel time from the current 5 hours to just 1.5 hours. The project also includes a new high-speed rail line along the same corridor. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Implement National Prenatal Screening Program for Genetic Diseases
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to introduce a unified prenatal screening system to detect fetal congenital malformations and chromosomal abnormalities early. The National Program 'Umut' for 2026-2030 has been approved. The new system will include ultrasound and biochemical screenings at specific gestational stages.

item.title: OIC Highlights Diplomatic Efforts and Continued Support for Afghanistan
item.description: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has emphasized its diplomatic engagement and ongoing support for Afghanistan. Ambassador Dr. Mohammed bin Saeed Al-Ayash delivered a lecture at the Diplomatic Institute of Afghanistan, detailing the OIC's history, institutions, and decisions concerning Afghanistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Amends Laws on Combating Extremism, Clarifies Definitions
item.description: Uzbekistan has amended its Criminal Code and Code of Administrative Offenses to enhance the fight against extremism. The new law, effective immediately, clarifies the definition of extremism and extremist activities, specifying actions that fall under this category, including attempts to forcibly alter constitutional order.

item.title: Tajik Parliament Speaker Visits Uzbekistan, Reviews 'New Tashkent' Project
item.description: Rustami Emomali, Chairman of Tajikistan's National Assembly and Mayor of Dushanbe, visited Uzbekistan on November 4, 2026. He laid a wreath at the Monument of Independence and reviewed the master plan for the 'New Tashkent' urban development project.

item.title: Analysts Note Mysterious Trading Surge Supporting Kazakhstan's Tenge
item.description: Halyk Finance analysts observed an unexplained increase in currency trading volume, potentially strengthening the Kazakh tenge. Trading volume rose 59.5% year-on-year to $78.8 billion in the first 10 months. High export revenues and non-resident capital inflows are cited as support.

item.title: Kazakh PM Criticizes Samruk-Kazyna Leadership Over Delayed Investment Projects
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov criticized the leadership of the Samruk-Kazyna Fund and its subsidiaries for the delayed implementation of certain investment projects. He stressed the need to increase the share of domestic content in goods and services procured for these projects.

item.title: New Bukhara Airport to Open by Independence Day 2027, President States
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyeyov has tasked officials to complete the new Bukhara airport and its accompanying BRT road by Independence Day in 2027. The $300 million airport will accommodate 20 aircraft and 1,200 passengers, with a new 24 km road connecting it to the city center.

item.title: Kazakh MP Calls Tokayev's Address Response to Public Expectations Amid Reforms
item.description: Kazakh Member of Parliament Aidоs Sarym stated that President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address to the nation fully meets public expectations and demands. He highlighted that Kazakhstan has implemented significant reforms despite a complex international situation, leading to a more active citizen participation in governance.

item.title: US judge temporarily halts deportation of detained Afghan nationals
item.description: A US federal judge has issued a temporary order blocking the deportation of detained Afghan nationals, citing risks to their lives. The order, effective until Saturday, follows concerns raised by members of Congress and human rights groups about potential persecution, torture, or death upon return to Afghanistan or Pakistan.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Criticizes Samruk-Kazyna Fund for Investment Project Delays
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has criticized the management of Samruk-Kazyna and its subsidiaries for delays in implementing investment projects. He instructed to strengthen control over project timelines and increase local content in procurement. The fund is currently implementing 69 large investment projects totaling 43.8 trillion tenge.

item.title: US Midterm Elections: Democrats Secure Control of Both Houses of Congress
item.description: Preliminary results from the US midterm elections indicate that Democrats have gained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives. Democrats have secured 53 seats in the Senate, exceeding the majority threshold, while Republicans hold 40 seats. In the House, Democrats have obtained the 218 seats needed for a majority.

item.title: Afghanistan-Pakistan Tensions Jeopardize Central and South Asian Trade Growth
item.description: Rising tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan are threatening efforts to expand trade and transport links between Central and South Asia. Strained relations undermine plans to strengthen commercial ties between Pakistan and Central Asian countries. Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have set ambitious trade targets, but face significant hurdles due to the instability.

item.title: Residents Seek Justice as Court Restricts Land Rights Acquired from Akimat
item.description: Residents of Sarykemer village in the Baizak district of Zhambyl region are concerned after a court imposed restrictions on land plots and houses they purchased from the akimat years ago. Despite obtaining legal documents and building homes, a recent court decision deemed the akimat's sale of the land illegal, raising fears of losing their properties.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Veterinarian Salaries and Establish Veterinary Chamber
item.description: Kazakhstan's parliament is considering a bill to raise veterinarian salaries and improve social protections. The average salary is expected to increase from approximately 220,000 to 420,000 tenge, potentially reaching 500,000 tenge with bonuses. The bill also proposes establishing a veterinary chamber to protect professionals' rights and interests.

item.title: Kazakhstan to borrow 227 billion tenge from Asian Development Bank
item.description: Kazakhstan will borrow 227.4 billion tenge (3.4 billion Chinese yuan) from the Asian Development Bank to cover budget expenditures. The loan, approved in two readings by parliament, has a 15-year term with a three-year grace period and an annual interest rate of 1.69%. The funds will be used for social sector development, infrastructure, industry, and education.

item.title: UNICEF Reports 19.2 Million Afghans Face Acute Hunger This Winter
item.description: UNICEF estimates 19.2 million people in Afghanistan will face acute food insecurity from November 2026 to April 2027. This includes approximately 5 million facing emergency levels of hunger. Child malnutrition is spreading, exacerbated by funding shortages threatening essential services.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Borrow 3.4 Billion Yuan from Asian Development Bank
item.description: Kazakhstan has opted for Chinese yuan for a new loan from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), citing rising interest rates on borrowing in Japanese yen, dollars, and euros. Finance Minister Madi Takiyev stated that the yuan loan offers stable rates and significant savings compared to domestic borrowing, with repayment over 15 years.

item.title: UN Rapporteur: Taliban Policies Severely Restrict Afghan Youth Opportunities
item.description: UN Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett stated that Taliban policies have significantly limited or eliminated higher education, career, financial independence, and public life opportunities for young Afghans. Despite aspirations to study, work, and contribute, many paths are now closed under Taliban rule, according to Bennett.

item.title: China Approves Import of Three Berry Types from Kyrgyzstan
item.description: China has officially permitted the import of raspberries, blackcurrants, and blackberries from Kyrgyzstan. This agreement, following a phytosanitary protocol signed in August 2026, opens new export opportunities for Kyrgyz producers in the large Chinese market. Producers must meet phytosanitary requirements and register their facilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Borrow Billions from ADB for Infrastructure and Industry
item.description: Kazakhstan will secure a loan of 3.4 billion Chinese yuan from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to finance transport infrastructure, industry, and education. The loan has a 15-year repayment term, including a three-year grace period, with an annual interest rate of 1.69%.

item.title: Lapid Accuses Netanyahu Allies of Attempting to Steal Election
item.description: Yair Lapid, a political opponent of Benjamin Netanyahu, warned that Netanyahu's allies are threatening to steal the election. Lapid stated this is an attempt to suppress democracy and steal the election with the help of government officials. Arab parties gained more seats in the recent election.

item.title: Democrats Gain Control of US Senate and House of Representatives
item.description: Democrats have regained control of the US Senate and House of Representatives following the midterm elections on November 3. Republicans previously held the majority in both chambers. Democrats secured at least eight seats in the House previously held by Republicans.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Maintains Key Rate at 14 Percent
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has kept its key interest rate unchanged at 14 percent. The bank cited high domestic demand and external market risks as reasons for maintaining tight monetary conditions and the attractiveness of national currency savings.

item.title: Trump Downplays Further Strikes on Iran, Cites US Preparedness
item.description: President Donald Trump has downplayed speculation of further US attacks on Iran post-midterm elections, stating the US is fully prepared. He indicated no immediate plans to attack Iran and suggested negotiations were yielding desired results, while noting pressure on Iran's economy.

item.title: Retail Price of Liquefied Gas to Increase in Uzbekistan
item.description: The retail price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) is set to rise in Uzbekistan. This price adjustment is expected to impact consumers across the country.

item.title: Environmentalists Inspect Shymkent Refinery Amid Resident Complaints
item.description: Environmentalists have inspected the Shymkent oil refinery following complaints from residents about air quality. Initial checks in October did not reveal any violations of permissible norms, despite reports of smog and chemical odors.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Reform Veterinary System with New Digital Platform and Support Measures
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to reform its veterinary system by expanding social support for specialists, enhancing industry control, and establishing a unified digital platform. A new bill, approved in its first reading, includes provisions for annual paid leave with health benefits and monthly bonuses for veterinary specialists with academic degrees. A veterinary chamber will also be created to represent professionals' interests.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Maintains Key Interest Rate at 14 Percent
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan's board decided to keep the main interest rate at an annual 14 percent during its November 4 meeting. While overall inflation slightly accelerated in September due to rising prices for fruits, vegetables, fuel, and services, core inflation remained stable. Inflation expectations for the next 12 months continue to decline for both the public and businesses.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Reduce Water Protection Zones for Tourist Facilities by Two-Thirds
item.description: Starting in 2027, Kyrgyzstan will reduce the minimum distance for tourist facilities from rivers from 75 to 25 meters as part of a pilot project. This change will apply only to structures made of lightweight materials and will require facilities to have their own sewage and local treatment systems. The initiative aims to support tourism development.

item.title: Kazakhstan plans to allocate 27 billion tenge annually for veterinary services
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to allocate approximately 27 billion tenge from the state budget each year to implement changes in veterinary legislation. These changes aim to provide additional social guarantees for veterinary specialists, including salary increases and improved working conditions. The bill also proposes the creation of a veterinary chamber and a pharmaceutical inspection to regulate veterinary drugs.

item.title: Afghanistan and Russia Discuss Expanding Trade and Investment Ties
item.description: Afghanistan and Russia have held discussions in Kabul aimed at strengthening bilateral trade, expanding private sector cooperation, and attracting new investment. The meeting between the Afghanistan Chamber of Commerce and Investment and the Russian Ambassador focused on boosting economic relations and creating more opportunities for businesses from both countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Tighten Regulations on Livestock Slaughter and Meat Sales
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to introduce stricter rules for livestock slaughter and meat sales. The proposed legislation aims to prevent the sale of meat from animals slaughtered outside designated areas and to enhance food safety. It also includes restrictions on using antibiotics in livestock intended for human consumption.
